dialogue.skyabyss.storyteller.fq_menu.co: Is anything troubling you about the hearth?
dialogue.skyabyss.storyteller.ms_coal_do: So this is from beneath... It's hot. Even after I let go, it's hot.

When I put it in the hearth, something answered at the bottom of the ash. ...An old coal came up.
You keep it. It seems to remember the fire below.
dialogue.skyabyss.storyteller.ms_coal_of:
The hearth? ...How did you know.
Lately the fire won't last until the seventh night. There used to be a coal at the bottom of the ash that never cooled.

They said it was a piece of the fire under the earth.
Not that anyone can go that far down. ...Could you?
dialogue.skyabyss.storyteller.ms_key: ...They came together, then. Let me see.
dialogue.skyabyss.storyteller.ms_key2:
The old tales call it the key to a door in the sky...
Strange. This key is beating downward.
dialogue.skyabyss.storyteller.ms_key3:
...Oh.
Five, five, a breath below the ground.
...That's how my mother sang the fifth. Why couldn't I remember it until now?
dialogue.skyabyss.storyteller.ms_key4:
Six and beyond still won't come.
...A key always turns toward the door it wants to open. Remember that much.
dialogue.skyabyss.storyteller.ms_thunder:
The second one. ...Side by side, they almost seem to pull at each other.
About the third, there's one thing I can think of.

On days of thunder, a great bird crosses inside the clouds. My grandmother said she stopped counting the day she saw it.
She never did tell me what she had been counting.
I'll climb a high peak and watch the sky.
What was she counting, I wonder?
The third one. ...Your hands smell a little scorched.
Only one left. ...Part of me wants to see them come together. Part of me doesn't.
I'll show you when they're together.
Who knows. ...People count from the flash to the thunder, don't they. Maybe that. Maybe not.
dialogue.skyabyss.storyteller.ms_tide_ba: Why, you smell of the sea. ...You found the second one, then?

So there was a heartbeat at the bottom of the sea, too.
In the sky, and in the sea. ...Things are beating all over the world, it seems.
dialogue.skyabyss.whale_chaser.fq_c_menu: Any clue about the next titan?
dialogue.skyabyss.whale_chaser.ms_c_cock:
Did a storm take it?
...My grandfather made one for every roof. There are still a few left.
dialogue.skyabyss.whale_chaser.ms_c_embe:
Once on the road I saw a mountain where the ash rose into the sky.
Even on nights without a fire anywhere, that mountain glowed a little red.

It isn't burning. It's smoldering, waiting.
The fourth is there, I think.
dialogue.skyabyss.whale_chaser.ms_c_key:
So that's... the key.
I always thought it opened a door in the sky. ...It's pointing down.
dialogue.skyabyss.whale_chaser.ms_c_key2:
I've spent my whole life looking up.
...I never once thought about what's under my feet.
dialogue.skyabyss.whale_chaser.ms_c_map_: The thunder came a long time after the flash.
I thought I saw the shape of wings in the lightning.

...I see. Something does cross along that line.
Take this scrap. I tore off just the part with the line.

And take this, too. My grandfather's weathercock.
Ever since he took it down from the roof, it points at storms instead of the wind.

Raise it somewhere high, and they say the storm takes notice.
...Not that I've ever tried.

A clue. ...Look at this. My old map.
I drew one line in the margin. Every time a storm comes, the clouds run along it.
On a thunder night, watch the sky from somewhere high. ...I just can't make myself go out when it thunders.
dialogue.skyabyss.whale_chaser.ms_c_thun:
The third. ...That one flew above the thundering clouds.
I was always afraid to look up at them. And you went there.
dialogue.skyabyss.whale_chaser.ms_c_tide:
You're back. ...Did you show the old woman the fragment?
I've heard it was split in four, too. One in the sky, one in the sea, they say.

By the sea, they say an island drifts to the shore at dawn and dusk. When the tide goes out.
...Do you think islands move? I don't.
Shall I count the low tides too?
You got onto the shelled mountain? ...How was it?
Its heartbeat rose and fell like the tide.
There was a town from the sea floor inside.

The whale sings in the sky, the turtle keeps the hours in the sea.
...As if they were both still doing what someone told them to, long ago.
item.skyabyss.keepsake.map_scrap: A Scrap of an Old Map
item.skyabyss.keepsake.map_scrap.lore: The corner of the whale chaser's map. A single thin line marks the path of the storms.
item.skyabyss.keepsake.warm_coal: A Coal That Will Not Cool
item.skyabyss.keepsake.warm_coal.lore: Found at the bottom of the storyteller's hearth. It stays faintly warm in your hand.
item.skyabyss.sky_key.desc: Four fragments made one. It does not point to the sky; it beats faintly toward the ground beneath you
lore.skyabyss.chapter1.ember.body:
Ash rises into the sky. Even on nights without a fire anywhere, that one mountain glows faintly red.

What I had taken for a mountain slowly drew a breath.
lore.skyabyss.chapter1.ember.title: The Ember Titan
lore.skyabyss.chapter1.fifth_verse.body:
The storyteller remembered it when she saw the sky key.

Five, five, a breath below the ground.

No one yet knows six, or what comes after.
lore.skyabyss.chapter1.fifth_verse.title: The Fifth Verse
lore.skyabyss.chapter1.sky_key_whole.bod:
When the four fragments touched in my hand, the seams faded away on their own, and they became a single key.

The old tales say it opens a door that leads above the clouds. Yet the key does not point to the sky. It beats faintly, toward somewhere far beneath my feet.
lore.skyabyss.chapter1.storm_path.body:
A single line is drawn in the margin of the whale chaser's old map. Whenever a storm comes, the clouds run along it.

From high ground on a thunder night, the lightning flashed along that line, one after another, always the same way. Something crosses by a fixed road.
lore.skyabyss.chapter1.storm_path.title: The Path of the Storms
lore.skyabyss.chapter1.thunder_wing.body:
In the instant lightning struck close by, there was a bird the size of a mountain beyond the curtain of rain.

Again and again the lightning struck the copper spikes of its crown. It did not so much as blink.
message.skyabyss.story.key_formed: The four fragments touched in your hand and became a single key.
message.skyabyss.story.key_formed_world: In %s's hand, the sky key took shape.
quest.skyabyss.daily_tide_rounds.done: It will be quiet inside the shell for a while.
A note on the board, the ink blurred by seawater: "The coral-haunted things are stirring again inside the Tide Shell's carapace. Put eight of them to rest."
Defeat coral thralls, scuttlers and puffers on the tide shell
quest.skyabyss.daily_tide_rounds.summary: Defeat eight coral thralls, reef scuttlers or bubble puffers on the tide shell's back. Party members count too.
quest.skyabyss.daily_tide_rounds.title: Rounds on the Tide Shell
quest.skyabyss.main_ember.done: The four fragments became one in my hands.
quest.skyabyss.main_ember.heart.journal:
What I took for a mountain is slowly breathing.
Inside its mouth lie three trial rooms and the smith; beyond them, a smoldering heartbeat. I'll still it.
quest.skyabyss.main_ember.heart.still: Go and still what beats inside the embers
quest.skyabyss.main_ember.key.journal: I have the fourth fragment. The fragments pull at each other in my hands.
quest.skyabyss.main_ember.rumor.journal:
Only one left. Isana has seen many things on his travels.
I'll go to his fire and ask.
quest.skyabyss.main_ember.see.journal: There is a mountain where the ash rises into the sky. Even on nights without fire, it glows faintly red.
quest.skyabyss.main_ember.summary: Head for the mountain where the ash rises into the sky, in search of the fourth fragment.
quest.skyabyss.main_ember.title: The Mountain Where Ash Rises
quest.skyabyss.main_key.done: The key is still beating downward.
quest.skyabyss.main_key.show.journal:
The key did not point above the clouds. It beats faintly, toward somewhere far beneath my feet.
I'll show it to the storyteller.
quest.skyabyss.main_key.show.talk: Go and show the storyteller the key
quest.skyabyss.main_key.summary: Show the storyteller the key that the fragments became.
quest.skyabyss.main_key.title: The Sky Key
quest.skyabyss.main_thunder.board.board: Ride the updraft on the peak
quest.skyabyss.main_thunder.board.journa:
the Thunder Wing Titan is said to come down onto the highest peak nearby. It always comes at the hour of the afternoon squall, but if I wait on the peak, it may notice me at any hour.
If I step into the column of wind at its feet, it may carry me up to its back.
quest.skyabyss.main_thunder.heart.journa:
Past the three trials and the raiju, below the keel, a heartbeat strikes like thunder.
The sound rises from below, not from above.
quest.skyabyss.main_thunder.heart.still: Go and still what beats behind the keel
quest.skyabyss.main_thunder.report.journ:
I have the third fragment. My hands smell faintly scorched.
Back to the village.
quest.skyabyss.main_thunder.report.st: Go and show the storyteller the fragment
quest.skyabyss.main_thunder.report.wc: Tell Isana what lies above the storm
quest.skyabyss.main_thunder.rumor.journa:
I have two fragments now. Side by side, they pull at each other a little.
I'll ask the storyteller about the third.
quest.skyabyss.main_thunder.rumor.talk: Ask the storyteller about the third
quest.skyabyss.main_thunder.see.journal:
On days of thunder, they say, a great bird crosses inside the clouds.
If I see a storm moving against the wind, that may be it.
quest.skyabyss.main_thunder.see.see: Find the storm against the wind
quest.skyabyss.main_thunder.summary: In search of the third fragment, chase the storm that moves against the wind and cross onto its back.
quest.skyabyss.main_thunder.title: Wings Across the Storm
quest.skyabyss.main_thunder.trials.journ:
Inside the bird's back, three trial rooms follow one after another.
The wind folk left inscriptions at their entrances. Cross all three and the way deeper should open.
quest.skyabyss.main_thunder.prepare.jour:
The storyteller said that to go to the storm bird, you must first know the lightning.
The ruin of the wind people's tower, the burnt tower on the slope, the stone under the peaks that lightning cannot pass. The traveller before you seems to have walked that road.
quest.skyabyss.main_thunder.prepare.lead: The storyteller: "If you mean to go into the storm, know the lightning first. The wind people left their marks on the peaks."
quest.skyabyss.main_thunder.prepare.read: Learn the lightning for the storm
quest.skyabyss.main_tide.board.board: Cross the gate at low tide
quest.skyabyss.main_tide.board.journal: There is an old gate on the rim of the shell, they say. It opens only when the tide is out.
quest.skyabyss.main_tide.done: Something beats in the sky, and in the sea.
quest.skyabyss.main_tide.heart.journal:
Past the three trials and the tide beckoner, deep in the shell, a heartbeat rises and falls like the tide.
The fragment must lie beside it.
quest.skyabyss.main_tide.heart.still: Go and still what beats deep in the shell
quest.skyabyss.main_tide.inscriptions.jo:
Inside the shell, three trial rooms follow one after another.
The people of the back left inscriptions at their entrances. Cross all three and go deeper.
quest.skyabyss.main_tide.inscriptions.re: Clear the trials, read their words
quest.skyabyss.main_tide.report.journal:
I have the second fragment. It seems to pull, faintly, toward the first.
I'll go back to the village and tell them.
quest.skyabyss.main_tide.report.st: Go and show the storyteller the fragment
quest.skyabyss.main_tide.report.wc: Tell Isana about the shelled mountain
quest.skyabyss.main_tide.rumor.journal:
The storyteller said the key was split in four. Do the other titans hold the rest?
Isana might have heard something.
quest.skyabyss.main_tide.see.journal:
They say an island comes to the shore when the tide goes out.
...Perhaps it isn't an island.
quest.skyabyss.main_tide.summary: Cross onto the back of the titan of the sea, in search of the second fragment.
quest.skyabyss.main_tide.title: The Gate of Ebb and Flow
quest.skyabyss.main_tide.prepare.journal:
Isana said that to cross to the island offshore, you must learn to read the tide. And you need a boat.
The vault at the end of the salt road is said to hold a carving on reading the tide. The wreck offshore holds a tide-watching shell.
quest.skyabyss.main_tide.prepare.lead: Isana: "If you mean to cross to the island, learn to read the tide first. And build a boat."
quest.skyabyss.main_tide.prepare.ready: Learn the tide and build a boat
quest.skyabyss.sub_old_map.done: The scrap of map shows a single line: the path of the storms. The weathercock always points at a storm.
quest.skyabyss.sub_old_map.summary: Watch the sky from somewhere high on a thunder night, and tell Isana about the path of the storms.
quest.skyabyss.sub_old_map.tell.journal:
I watched the sky from up high on a thunder night.
I'll go and tell Isana.
quest.skyabyss.sub_old_map.tell.talk: Tell Isana about the stormy sky
quest.skyabyss.sub_old_map.title: The Whale Chaser's Old Map
quest.skyabyss.sub_old_map.watch.journal:
A single line is drawn in the margin of Isana's old map. Every storm, the clouds run along it.
On a thunder night, I'll watch the sky from somewhere high.
quest.skyabyss.sub_old_map.watch.storm: Stand somewhere high under open sky (height 100+) during a thunderstorm
quest.skyabyss.sub_warm_coal.done: The coal from the bottom of the ash stays warm.
quest.skyabyss.sub_warm_coal.fetch.journ:
The storyteller's hearth won't last to the seventh night. There was once a piece of 'fire from beneath the earth' in the ash.
Beneath the earth... In the Nether, I might find a fire that won't cool.
quest.skyabyss.sub_warm_coal.summary: Bring back a piece of the fire beneath the earth for the storyteller's hearth.
quest.skyabyss.sub_warm_coal.tell.journa:
I have four pieces of a fire that won't cool.
I'll take them to the storyteller's hearth.
quest.skyabyss.sub_warm_coal.tell.talk: Give the storyteller the pieces of fire
quest.skyabyss.sub_warm_coal.title: The Coal That Will Not Cool
quest.skyabyss.weekly_tide_heart.done: The ebb and flow has stopped. But the tide will come in again, surely.
quest.skyabyss.weekly_tide_heart.heart.j: A note in the corner of the board, in the same unsigned hand: "The tide fills in seven days. Go and make sure, before it is full."
quest.skyabyss.weekly_tide_heart.summary: Still the tide shell's heart once more. Party members in the fight count too.
quest.skyabyss.weekly_tide_heart.title: The Tide's Heart, Once More
scene.skyabyss.sky_key.end_hint: Esc or click to return  (titan backs and requests remain open)
scene.skyabyss.sky_key.end_sub: This is the end of the beta
scene.skyabyss.sky_key.end_title: The Titan Arc: The Sky Key
scene.skyabyss.sky_key.line1: The four fragments touched in your hand.
scene.skyabyss.sky_key.line2: The seams fade away on their own.
scene.skyabyss.sky_key.line3: The key does not point to the sky.
scene.skyabyss.sky_key.line4: Far beneath your feet, something is slowly beating.
scene.skyabyss.sky_key.title: The Sky Key
chapter.skyabyss.aftermath.head: %s: Complete
chapter.skyabyss.aftermath.preview: This heartbeat was only borrowed from the depths.
quest.skyabyss.main_ember.prepare.journa:
Isana said that to go to the burning mountain, you must first be ready for the fire.
The artisan knows how to make a fire-ward draught, and the storyteller knows of the ash folk's old forge.
quest.skyabyss.main_ember.prepare.lead: Isana: "If you mean to go to the burning mountain, get ready for the fire first. Go and see the artisan and the storyteller."
quest.skyabyss.main_ember.prepare.ready: Get ready for the mountain of fire
